correctness.rationale: The graph-vertex/maximal-clique incidence structure of a connected block graph is a tree. For every clique, the selected set is none, singleton, or all, because an outside clique vertex may not have two selected neighbors. Conditioned on a parent vertex, selected state A and two unselected states B0/B1 (0 or 1 selected descendant neighbors) suffice; α=∏B0+∏A, β=∏(B0+B1), γ=∑_u A_u∏_{w≠u}B0_w are exhaustive disjoint block transitions. Parent vertex transitions A=x∏α, B0=∏β, B1=∑_Bγ_B∏_{C≠B}β_C count each legal labeling once by rooted-tree induction. Two-state product/sum accumulators cost O(total clique incidences)=O(n) arithmetic gates, independent of clique size; block decomposition O(n+e). Independent exhaustive subset enumeration agreed with reconstructed recurrences for 20 small glued-block graphs of <=11 vertices. Special one-vertex and bridge cases satisfy the same empty-product conventions.
